#Setup for Data Analysis

```{r}
# Dataset: Heart Failure Clinical Records


library(tidyverse)
library(e1071)      # For skewness calculations
library(corrr)      # For tidy correlation matrices
library(car)        # For VIF calculation via glm
library(gridExtra)  # For side-by-side ggplot arranging

#loading and cleaning data
df <- read_csv("heart_failure_data.csv")

# Overview of data types and dimensions
#cat("=== DATASET STRUCTURE ===\n")
#glimpse(df)

# Check for missing values across all columns
#missing_summary <- colSums(is.na(df))
#cat("\n=== MISSING VALUES PER VARIABLE ===\n")
#print(missing_summary)

# Encode categorical binary variables as factors for clarity
df_clean <- df %>%
  mutate(
    anaemia             = factor(anaemia, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    diabetes            = factor(diabetes, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    high_blood_pressure = factor(high_blood_pressure, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    sex                 = factor(sex, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    smoking             = factor(smoking, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    DEATH_EVENT         = factor(DEATH_EVENT, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Survived", "Died"))
  )

#summary statistics
continuous_vars <- c("age", "creatinine_phosphokinase", "ejection_fraction", 
                      "platelets", "serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium", "time")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(moments)

summary_stats <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(continuous_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n        = sum(!is.na(value)),
    mean     = base::mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd       = stats::sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median   = stats::median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR      = stats::IQR(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min      = base::min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max      = base::max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    skewness = moments::skewness(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    skew_label = case_when(
      abs(skewness) < 0.5 ~ "Fairly Symmetric",
      abs(skewness) >= 0.5 & abs(skewness) <= 1 ~ "Moderately Skewed",
      abs(skewness) > 1 ~ "Highly Skewed"
    )
  )

print(summary_stats)
```

#Box-Cox Transformations of Variables

```{r}
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)

# Function to compute Box-Cox transform for a single vector
apply_boxcox_vector <- function(x) {
  # Shift non-positive values if any exist
  shift <- if (min(x, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) abs(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) + 0.001 else 0
  x_pos <- x + shift
  
  # Find optimal lambda
  bc <- boxcox(x_pos ~ 1, plotit = FALSE)
  opt_lambda <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
  
  # Apply transformation
  if (abs(opt_lambda) < 1e-4) {
    transformed <- log(x_pos)
  } else {
    transformed <- (x_pos^opt_lambda - 1) / opt_lambda
  }
  
  attr(transformed, "lambda") <- opt_lambda
  return(transformed)
}

# Apply to all continuous variables and create new transformed columns
df_boxcox_transformed <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(across(
    .cols = all_of(continuous_vars),
    .fns = apply_boxcox_vector,
    .names = "bc_{.col}"
  ))

# Print estimated lambdas
lambdas <- sapply(df_boxcox_transformed[paste0("bc_", continuous_vars)], function(col) attr(col, "lambda"))
print(lambdas)


library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

get_boxcox_ci <- function(x, conf_level = 0.95) {
  # Shift non-positive values if present
  shift <- if (min(x, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) abs(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) + 0.001 else 0
  x_pos <- x + shift
  
  # Compute profile log-likelihood
  bc <- boxcox(x_pos ~ 1, plotit = FALSE)
  
  # Point estimate (max log-likelihood)
  max_loglik <- max(bc$y)
  opt_lambda <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
  
  # Chi-squared cutoff threshold for confidence interval
  limit <- max_loglik - 0.5 * qchisq(conf_level, df = 1)
  
  # Filter lambda values within cutoff
  ci_lambdas <- bc$x[bc$y >= limit]
  lambda_low  <- min(ci_lambdas)
  lambda_high <- max(ci_lambdas)
  
  return(tibble(
    lambda_hat = round(opt_lambda, 3),
    ci_lower   = round(lambda_low, 3),
    ci_upper   = round(lambda_high, 3),
    ci_95      = paste0("[", round(lambda_low, 2), ", ", round(lambda_high, 2), "]")
  ))
}

# Calculate CIs across all continuous variables
continuous_vars <- c("age", "creatinine_phosphokinase", "ejection_fraction", 
                       "platelets", "serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium", "time")

ci_summary <- map_dfr(continuous_vars, ~ {
  get_boxcox_ci(df_clean[[.x]]) %>%
    mutate(variable = .x, .before = 1)
})

print(ci_summary)
```

#Applying the Box-Cox Recommended Transforms

```{r}
library(dplyr)

df_clean <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # Log transformation for age (\lambda \approx 0)
    log_age = log(age),
    
    # Power transform (-0.2) for creatinine phosphokinase
    cpk_pow_neg02 = creatinine_phosphokinase^(-0.2),
    
    # Cube root transformation (\lambda \approx 0.33) for ejection fraction
    ef_cbrt = ejection_fraction^(1/3),
    
    # Square root transformation (\lambda = 0.5) for platelets
    sqrt_platelets = sqrt(platelets),
    
    # Inverse / -1 power transformation (\lambda = -1) for serum creatinine
    inv_serum_creatinine = 1 / serum_creatinine,
    
    # Square transformation (\lambda = 2) for serum sodium
    sq_serum_sodium = serum_sodium^2,
    
    # Square root transformation (\lambda \approx 0.5) for follow-up time
    sqrt_time = sqrt(time)
  )

df_clean


cont_vars <- c("log_age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ef_cbrt", "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "sq_serum_sodium", "sqrt_time")
```

#Outlier Detection From the Original to Box-Cox Transformed Variables

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

#define feature sets
orig_vars <- c("age", "creatinine_phosphokinase", "ejection_fraction", 
               "platelets", "serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium", "time")

bc_vars   <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
               "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium", "sqrt_time")

#helper function to calculate outlier diagnostics for a single vector
get_outlier_stats <- function(x, var_name, var_type) {
  x_clean <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n_total <- length(x_clean)
  
  # IQR Bounds (Tukey's Fences)
  q25 <- stats::quantile(x_clean, 0.25)
  q75 <- stats::quantile(x_clean, 0.75)
  iqr_val <- q75 - q25
  
  iqr_lower_1.5 <- q25 - 1.5 * iqr_val
  iqr_upper_1.5 <- q75 + 1.5 * iqr_val
  iqr_lower_3.0 <- q25 - 3.0 * iqr_val
  iqr_upper_3.0 <- q75 + 3.0 * iqr_val
  
  n_iqr_1.5 <- sum(x_clean < iqr_lower_1.5 | x_clean > iqr_upper_1.5)
  n_iqr_3.0 <- sum(x_clean < iqr_lower_3.0 | x_clean > iqr_upper_3.0)
  
  # Z-Score Bounds (|Z| > 3)
  mean_val <- base::mean(x_clean)
  sd_val   <- stats::sd(x_clean)
  z_scores <- (x_clean - mean_val) / sd_val
  n_z3     <- sum(abs(z_scores) > 3)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    type             = var_type,
    variable         = var_name,
    n_obs            = n_total,
    iqr_outliers_1.5 = n_iqr_1.5,
    pct_iqr_1.5      = round((n_iqr_1.5 / n_total) * 100, 2),
    iqr_outliers_3.0 = n_iqr_3.0,
    pct_iqr_3.0      = round((n_iqr_3.0 / n_total) * 100, 2),
    z_outliers_3     = n_z3,
    pct_z_3          = round((n_z3 / n_total) * 100, 2)
  )
}

# Run diagnostics on original variables
orig_diagnostics <- purrr::map_dfr(orig_vars, ~ get_outlier_stats(df_clean[[.x]], .x, "Original"))

# Run diagnostics on Box-Cox transformed variables
bc_diagnostics   <- purrr::map_dfr(bc_vars, ~ get_outlier_stats(df_clean[[.x]], .x, "Box-Cox Transformed"))

# Combine results into a comparison table
outlier_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(orig_diagnostics, bc_diagnostics)

cat("=== OUTLIER DIAGNOSTICS COMPARISON ===\n")
print(outlier_summary, n = 20)


# Side-by-side comparison for corresponding variables
comparison_table <- tibble::tibble(
  metric                   = c("CPK", "Serum Creatinine", "Platelets", "Time"),
  Original_Variable        = c("creatinine_phosphokinase", "serum_creatinine", "platelets", "time"),
  BoxCox_Variable          = c("cpk_pow_neg02", "inv_serum_creatinine", "sqrt_platelets", "sqrt_time")
) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(orig_diagnostics %>% dplyr::select(Original_Variable = variable, Orig_IQR_1.5 = iqr_outliers_1.5, Orig_Z3 = z_outliers_3), by = "Original_Variable") %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(bc_diagnostics %>% dplyr::select(BoxCox_Variable = variable, BC_IQR_1.5 = iqr_outliers_1.5, BC_Z3 = z_outliers_3), by = "BoxCox_Variable")

print(comparison_table)
```




#Table Summarizing Variables Across Both Dead/Surviving Patients

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)


#continuous variables summary by death event
cont_summary <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(DEATH_EVENT, all_of(continuous_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(continuous_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(DEATH_EVENT, variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n             = sum(!is.na(value)),
    mean          = base::mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd            = stats::sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median        = stats::median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Parametric 95% CI for the Mean
    mean_ci_lower = mean - 1.96 * (sd / sqrt(n)),
    mean_ci_upper = mean + 1.96 * (sd / sqrt(n)),
    # Empirical 95% Percentile Bounds (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of sample)
    emp_p2.5      = stats::quantile(value, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    emp_p97.5     = stats::quantile(value, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_sd   = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean, sd),
    mean_95ci = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", mean_ci_lower, mean_ci_upper),
    emp_95ci  = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", emp_p2.5, emp_p97.5)
  )

#reshape into table
cont_table_formatted <- cont_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, DEATH_EVENT, mean_sd, median, mean_95ci, emp_95ci) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = DEATH_EVENT,
    values_from = c(mean_sd, median, mean_95ci, emp_95ci)
  )


binary_vars <- binary_variables
#binary variable summary by death event
binary_summary <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(DEATH_EVENT, dplyr::all_of(binary_vars)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = dplyr::all_of(binary_vars), 
    names_to  = "variable", 
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(DEATH_EVENT, variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_group = dplyr::n(),
    count_yes   = base::sum(value == "Yes" | value == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_yes     = (count_yes / total_group) * 100,
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_label = base::sprintf("%.1f%% (%d/%d)", pct_yes, count_yes, total_group)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, DEATH_EVENT, pct_label) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = DEATH_EVENT, 
    values_from = pct_label
  )

cat("\n=== BINARY VARIABLES PREVALENCE (% YES) BY SURVIVAL STATUS ===\n")
print(binary_summary)

#reshape into table
cont_table_clean <- cont_summary %>%   dplyr::select(variable, DEATH_EVENT, mean_sd, median, emp_95ci) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = DEATH_EVENT,
    values_from = c(mean_sd, median, emp_95ci),
    names_glue  = "Group_{DEATH_EVENT}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    variable,
    Survived_Mean_SD = Group_0_mean_sd,
    Survived_Median  = Group_0_median,
    Survived_95CI    = Group_0_emp_95ci,
    Died_Mean_SD     = Group_1_mean_sd,
    Died_Median      = Group_1_median,
    Died_95CI        = Group_1_emp_95ci
  )

print(cont_table_clean)
```

#Variance Inflation Factor Diagnostics #No high variation inflation for any predictor

```{r}
library(car)

# Define binary predictors
binary_vars <- c("anaemia", "diabetes", "high_blood_pressure", "smoking")

# Fit baseline logistic regression model including all continuous and binary predictors
formula_vif <- as.formula(
  paste("DEATH_EVENT ~", paste(c(cont_vars_model, binary_vars), collapse = " + "))
)

model_vif <- glm(formula_vif, data = df_clean, family = binomial)

# Compute VIF
vif_values <- car::vif(model_vif)

vif_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  predictor = names(vif_values),
  VIF       = as.numeric(vif_values)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    multicollinearity = dplyr::case_when(
      VIF < 5 ~ "Low (Acceptable)",
      VIF >= 5 & VIF < 10 ~ "Moderate",
      VIF >= 10 ~ "High (Severe)"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(VIF))

cat("=== VARIANCE INFLATION FACTOR (VIF) DIAGNOSTICS ===\n")
print(vif_summary)
```

#Scaling Variables + Perform PCA

```{r}
library(dplyr)

#continuous variables in the model
cont_vars_model <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
                     "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium")

#perform PCA
x_mat <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cont_vars_model))

pca_res <- prcomp(x_mat, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Variance Explained Summary
var_explained <- pca_res$sdev^2
prop_var      <- var_explained / sum(var_explained)
cum_var       <- cumsum(prop_var)

pca_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Component        = paste0("PC", 1:length(prop_var)),
  Standard_Dev     = pca_res$sdev,
  Variance_Ratio   = round(prop_var, 4),
  Cumulative_Ratio = round(cum_var, 4)
)

cat("=== PCA VARIANCE EXPLAINED SUMMARY ===\n")
print(pca_summary)
```

#PCA Scree Plot + Cummulative Variance Visualization

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Create Scree plot dataframe
scree_df <- data.frame(
  PC = factor(paste0("PC", 1:length(prop_var)), levels = paste0("PC", 1:length(prop_var))),
  PropVar = prop_var,
  CumVar = cum_var
)

# Scree Plot
ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = PC)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = PropVar), fill = "#2b5c8f", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = CumVar, group = 1), color = "#d95f02", size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = CumVar), color = "#d95f02", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Scree Plot & Cumulative Variance Explained",
    x = "Principal Component",
    y = "Proportion / Cumulative Variance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#PC Pair Scatter PLots Stratified By Outcome

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)

# Extract scores for top 5 components and add outcome labels
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:5]) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = factor(df_clean$DEATH_EVENT, labels = c("Survived (0)", "Died (1)"))
  )

# Calculate variance explained percentages for labels
pc_pct <- round(prop_var[1:5] * 100, 1)

# Generate all 10 pairwise combinations
pairs <- utils::combn(1:5, 2, simplify = FALSE)


# Helper function to generate a single PC scatter plot
plot_pc_pair <- function(pair) {
  i <- pair[1]
  j <- pair[2]
  
  x_col <- paste0("PC", i)
  y_col <- paste0("PC", j)
  
  ggplot(pca_scores, aes_string(x = x_col, y = y_col, color = "Outcome")) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.65, size = 1.5) +
    stat_ellipse(level = 0.68, linetype = 2, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Survived (0)" = "#2166ac", "Died (1)" = "#b2182b")) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("PC", i, " vs PC", j),
      x     = paste0("PC", i, " (", pc_pct[i], "%)"),
      y     = paste0("PC", j, " (", pc_pct[j], "%)")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      axis.title   = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# Generate plot lists for each batch of 5
```

#Clustering: Select Number of Groups #All sillhouette widths are fairly small (\<.16) indicating that no substantial cluster structure is contained in the continuous feature space #Choosing k=2 or 3 allows for discrimination into low/medium/high risk groups, but greater than that results in over-segmentation due to small sample size with little clinical seperation. #The results indicate the perhaps supervised classification models would be better suited to capture mortality risk.

```{r}

  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cont_vars_model)) %>%

#elbow method for K-means (WSS)
```

#Perform Clustering for k=2, 3

```{r}
library(cluster)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(42)

#k-means clustering (k = 2 and k = 3) ---
kmeans_k2 <- kmeans(df_scaled, centers = 2, nstart = 25)
kmeans_k3 <- kmeans(df_scaled, centers = 3, nstart = 25)

#k-medians / PAM clustering (k = 2 and k = 3) ---
#PAM uses manhattan distance for medoid calculation
pam_k2 <- cluster::pam(df_scaled, k = 2, metric = "manhattan")
pam_k3 <- cluster::pam(df_scaled, k = 3, metric = "manhattan")

# Attach cluster assignments back to df_clean
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    kmeans_cluster_k2 = factor(kmeans_k2$cluster),
    kmeans_cluster_k3 = factor(kmeans_k3$cluster),
    pam_cluster_k2    = factor(pam_k2$clustering),
    pam_cluster_k3    = factor(pam_k3$clustering)
  )

#function for cluster summaries
get_cluster_summary <- function(data, cluster_col) {
  data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Cluster = .data[[cluster_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      N              = dplyr::n(),
      Deaths         = sum(DEATH_EVENT == 1),
      Mortality_Rate = paste0(round(mean(DEATH_EVENT) * 100, 1), "%"),
      .groups        = "drop"
    )
}

cat("=== K-MEANS (k = 2) MORTALITY BREAKDOWN ===\n")
print(get_cluster_summary(df_clean, "kmeans_cluster_k2"))

cat("\n=== K-MEANS (k = 3) MORTALITY BREAKDOWN ===\n")
print(get_cluster_summary(df_clean, "kmeans_cluster_k3"))

cat("\n=== K-MEDIANS / PAM (k = 2) MORTALITY BREAKDOWN ===\n")
print(get_cluster_summary(df_clean, "pam_cluster_k2"))

cat("\n=== K-MEDIANS / PAM (k = 3) MORTALITY BREAKDOWN ===\n")
print(get_cluster_summary(df_clean, "pam_cluster_k3"))
```

#MANOVA Test + Hotellings T\^2 Test 
#The joiny physiological profies of survival vs. deceased groups differ significantly in 6-dimensional continuous feature space

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(Hotelling)

#define transformed continuous predictors (excluding time to avoid target leakage)
cont_vars_transformed <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
                           "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium")

#extract feature matrix and outcome
Y_mat <- as.matrix(df_clean[, cont_vars_transformed])
group <- factor(df_clean$DEATH_EVENT, labels = c("Survived", "Died"))

#fit MANOVA
manova_fit <- manova(Y_mat ~ group)

#display test statistics
cat("=== MANOVA TEST STATISTICS ===\n")
print(summary(manova_fit, test = "Pillai"))
print(summary(manova_fit, test = "Wilks"))
print(summary(manova_fit, test = "Hotelling-Lawley"))

#hotelling T^2 test
#split matrix by outcome groups
Y_survived <- Y_mat[group == "Survived", ]
Y_died     <- Y_mat[group == "Died", ]

hotelling_res <- Hotelling::hotelling.test(Y_survived, Y_died)

cat("\n=== HOTELLING'S T^2 TEST RESULT ===\n")
print(hotelling_res)
```

#Logistic Regression with main effects only
```{r}
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(pROC)
library(broom)

set.seed(42)

#stratified 80/20 train/test split
train_index <- caret::createDataPartition(df_clean$DEATH_EVENT, p = 0.80, list = FALSE)

train_df <- df_clean[train_index, ]
test_df  <- df_clean[-train_index, ]

#fit logistic regression on strictly cont_vars_model features
logit_formula <- DEATH_EVENT ~ age + cpk_pow_neg02 + ejection_fraction + 
                 sqrt_platelets + inv_serum_creatinine + serum_sodium + anaemia + diabetes + high_blood_pressure+ smoking

glm_fit <- glm(logit_formula, data = train_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

#model summary and odds ratio
cat("=== LOGISTIC REGRESSION MODEL SUMMARY ===\n")
print(summary(glm_fit))

or_summary <- broom::tidy(glm_fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Term = term,
    `Odds Ratio (OR)` = estimate,
    `2.5 %` = conf.low,
    `97.5 %` = conf.high,
    `p-value` = p.value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

cat("\n=== ODDS RATIOS & 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVALS ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(or_summary))

#predict on test set, calculate accuracy
test_probs <- predict(glm_fit, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
test_preds <- ifelse(test_probs >= 0.5, 1, 0)

pred_factor <- factor(test_preds, levels = c(0, 1))
true_factor <- factor(test_df$DEATH_EVENT, levels = c(0, 1))

cm_obj <- caret::confusionMatrix(pred_factor, true_factor, positive = "1")

#extract roc-auc
roc_obj  <- pROC::roc(test_df$DEATH_EVENT, test_probs, quiet = TRUE)
test_auc <- pROC::auc(roc_obj)

cat("\n=== TEST SET PERFORMANCE ===\n")
cat("ROC-AUC    :", round(test_auc, 4), "\n")
print(cm_obj$overall[c("Accuracy", "AccuracyLower", "AccuracyUpper", "AccuracyPValue")])

cat("\n=== DETAILED CONFUSION MATRIX & METRICS ===\n")
print(cm_obj)
```

#Logistic Regression with Main Effects + Two Way Interactions Best Model by AIC/BIC
```{r}
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)

#define formula with main effects and all 2-way interactions
interaction_formula <- DEATH_EVENT ~ (age + cpk_pow_neg02 + ejection_fraction + 
                 sqrt_platelets + inv_serum_creatinine + serum_sodium + anaemia + diabetes + high_blood_pressure+ smoking)^2

#fit full model (main effects + 2 way interactions) on training data
full_interaction_model <- glm(interaction_formula, data = train_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
null_model              <- glm(DEATH_EVENT ~ 1, data = train_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

#aic subset selection
best_model_aic <- MASS::stepAIC(
  null_model,
  scope     = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_interaction_model),
  direction = "both",
  trace     = FALSE
)

#bic subset selection
n_train        <- nrow(train_df)
best_model_bic <- MASS::stepAIC(
  null_model,
  scope     = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_interaction_model),
  direction = "both",
  k         = log(n_train),
  trace     = FALSE
)

#model summaries
cat("=== BEST SUBSET MODEL SELECTED BY AIC ===\n")
print(summary(best_model_aic))

cat("\n=== BEST SUBSET MODEL SELECTED BY BIC ===\n")
print(summary(best_model_bic))

library(caret)
library(pROC)

evaluate_subset_model <- function(model, name, test_data) {
  probs <- predict(model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
  preds <- ifelse(probs >= 0.5, 1, 0)
  
  pred_f <- factor(preds, levels = c(0, 1))
  true_f <- factor(test_data$DEATH_EVENT, levels = c(0, 1))
  
  cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(pred_f, true_f, positive = "1")
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(test_data$DEATH_EVENT, probs, quiet = TRUE)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model       = name,
    AIC         = round(AIC(model), 2),
    BIC         = round(BIC(model), 2),
    Parameters  = length(coef(model)),
    Test_Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4),
    Test_AUC    = round(pROC::auc(roc_obj), 4),
    Sensitivity = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Specificity = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 4)
  )
}

# Compare performance across models
comp_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  evaluate_subset_model(best_model_aic, "Best Subset (AIC)", test_df),
  evaluate_subset_model(best_model_bic, "Best Subset (BIC)", test_df)
)

cat("=== SUBSET MODEL PERFORMANCE COMPARISON ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(comp_table))
```

```{r}
#visualization
format_vif <- function(vif_out, model_name) {
  if (is.matrix(vif_out)) {
    df_vif <- as.data.frame(vif_out)
    df_vif$Term <- rownames(df_vif)
    df_vif$Adjusted_VIF <- df_vif$`GVIF^(1/(2*Df))`^2  # Square to put back on standard VIF scale
  } else {
    df_vif <- data.frame(
      Term = names(vif_out),
      GVIF = as.numeric(vif_out),
      `GVIF^(1/(2*Df))` = sqrt(as.numeric(vif_out)),
      Adjusted_VIF = as.numeric(vif_out),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
  df_vif$Model <- model_name
  return(df_vif)
}

df_vif_bic <- format_vif(vif_bic, "BIC Model (Main Effects)")
df_vif_aic <- format_vif(vif_aic, "AIC Model (With Interactions)")

vif_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(df_vif_bic, df_vif_aic)

#plot adjusted vif values
ggplot(vif_combined, aes(x = reorder(Term, Adjusted_VIF), y = Adjusted_VIF, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dotted", color = "darkred", size = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("BIC Model (Main Effects)" = "#2b5c8f", "AIC Model (With Interactions)" = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(
    title = "Multicollinearity Diagnostics Across Logistic Models",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = Moderately High Multicollinearity (VIF = 5)",
    x = "Model Term",
    y = "Adjusted VIF / (GVIF^(1/(2*df)))^2",
    fill = "Model Architecture"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

#Determining Optimal Deceision Threshold in the Logistic Regression and Model Evaluation
#The Models from above had high specificity but low sensitivity likely due to unbalanced number of deaths appearing in the data
#We find that for clinical settings having a high sensitivity helps identify mortality risks which the BIC model with Youden J Threshold (0.224) chosen #selects this. The AIC model with the Down Sampled Train is a follow up since it maximizes the ROC_AUC but it lacks as much sensitivity.
```{r}
library(pROC)
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

#function to evaluate the models
eval_metrics <- function(probs, actual, threshold = 0.5, model_name, approach_name) {
  preds <- ifelse(probs >= threshold, 1, 0)
  
  pred_f <- factor(preds, levels = c(0, 1))
  true_f <- factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1))
  
  cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(pred_f, true_f, positive = "1")
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(actual, probs, quiet = TRUE)
  
  # Confusion matrix elements for MCC
  TP <- cm$table["1", "1"]
  TN <- cm$table["0", "0"]
  FP <- cm$table["1", "0"]
  FN <- cm$table["0", "1"]
  
  num <- (TP * TN) - (FP * FN)
  den <- sqrt(as.numeric(TP + FP) * as.numeric(TP + FN) * 
              as.numeric(TN + FP) * as.numeric(TN + FN))
  
  mcc_val <- ifelse(den == 0, 0, num / den)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model            = model_name,
    Approach         = approach_name,
    Threshold        = round(threshold, 4),
    Sensitivity      = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Specificity      = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 4),
    MCC              = round(mcc_val, 4),
    Overall_Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4),
    ROC_AUC          = round(pROC::auc(roc_obj), 4)
  )
}


#evaluate baseline and optimization via youden's j statistic

# Probabilities on test set
probs_aic <- predict(best_model_aic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
probs_bic <- predict(best_model_bic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")

# Optimal thresholds via Youden's J
opt_thresh_aic <- pROC::coords(pROC::roc(test_df$DEATH_EVENT, probs_aic, quiet = TRUE), "best", best.method = "youden")$threshold
opt_thresh_bic <- pROC::coords(pROC::roc(test_df$DEATH_EVENT, probs_bic, quiet = TRUE), "best", best.method = "youden")$threshold

# Compute Metrics for Baseline and Approach A
res_baseline_aic <- eval_metrics(probs_aic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, 0.5000, "AIC Model", "1. Baseline (p = 0.50)")
res_youden_aic   <- eval_metrics(probs_aic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, opt_thresh_aic, "AIC Model", "2. Youden J Threshold")

res_baseline_bic <- eval_metrics(probs_bic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, 0.5000, "BIC Model", "1. Baseline (p = 0.50)")
res_youden_bic   <- eval_metrics(probs_bic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, opt_thresh_bic, "BIC Model", "2. Youden J Threshold")


#balancing training data approach
set.seed(42)

#down sampled training data
train_balanced <- caret::downSample(
  x = train_df[, c("inv_serum_creatinine", "age", "ejection_fraction")],
  y = factor(train_df$DEATH_EVENT),
  yname = "DEATH_EVENT"
)
train_balanced$DEATH_EVENT <- as.numeric(as.character(train_balanced$DEATH_EVENT))

#refit models on balanced data
aic_formula <- DEATH_EVENT ~ inv_serum_creatinine + age + ejection_fraction + 
               inv_serum_creatinine:ejection_fraction + age:ejection_fraction

bic_formula <- DEATH_EVENT ~ inv_serum_creatinine + age + ejection_fraction

glm_bal_aic <- glm(aic_formula, data = train_balanced, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
glm_bal_bic <- glm(bic_formula, data = train_balanced, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

#predict on test set
probs_bal_aic <- predict(glm_bal_aic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
probs_bal_bic <- predict(glm_bal_bic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")

#compute metrics for balanced approach
res_bal_aic <- eval_metrics(probs_bal_aic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, 0.5000, "AIC Model", "3. Down-Sampled Train")
res_bal_bic <- eval_metrics(probs_bal_bic, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, 0.5000, "BIC Model", "3. Down-Sampled Train")

#summary table
comparison_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  res_baseline_aic, res_youden_aic, res_bal_aic,
  res_baseline_bic, res_youden_bic, res_bal_bic
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Model, Approach)

cat("=== COMPREHENSIVE PERFORMANCE COMPARISON: AIC VS BIC MODELS ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(comparison_table))
```



#Random Forest Model Training to See if Non-Linear Feature Spaces Can Outperform Logistic Regression
```{r}
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(42)

#prepare factor target variable for Random Forest classification
train_df_rf <- train_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DEATH_EVENT_FACTOR = factor(DEATH_EVENT, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Survived", "Died")))

test_df_rf <- test_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DEATH_EVENT_FACTOR = factor(DEATH_EVENT, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Survived", "Died")))

#fit random forest model (using the 6 transformed continuous predictors)
rf_formula <- DEATH_EVENT_FACTOR ~ age + cpk_pow_neg02 + ejection_fraction + 
              sqrt_platelets + inv_serum_creatinine + serum_sodium + anaemia + diabetes + smoking + high_blood_pressure

rf_fit <- randomForest::randomForest(
  rf_formula,
  data = train_df_rf,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 2,           # sqrt(p) ~ 2 for 6 predictors
  importance = TRUE,
  proximity = TRUE
)

cat("=== RANDOM FOREST MODEL (OOB ESTIMATES) ===\n")
print(rf_fit)
```

#Handle Settng Optimal Decision Threshold
```{r}
#predict probabilities on the test set for class 'Died' (DEATH_EVENT = 1)
test_rf_probs <- predict(rf_fit, newdata = test_df_rf, type = "prob")[, "Died"]

#extract roc-auc and optimal youden's j threshold
roc_rf <- pROC::roc(test_df$DEATH_EVENT, test_rf_probs, quiet = TRUE)
opt_thresh_rf <- pROC::coords(roc_rf, "best", best.method = "youden")$threshold

cat("=== RANDOM FOREST TEST EVALUATION ===\n")
cat("Test ROC-AUC            :", round(pROC::auc(roc_rf), 4), "\n")
cat("Optimal Youden Threshold:", round(opt_thresh_rf, 4), "\n\n")

#function to build confusion matrix & calculate metrics (with MCC)
get_rf_metrics <- function(probs, actual, threshold, label) {
  preds <- ifelse(probs >= threshold, 1, 0)
  cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(
    factor(preds, levels = c(0, 1)),
    factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1)),
    positive = "1"
  )
  
  #extract confusion matrix values for MCC
  TP <- cm$table["1", "1"]
  TN <- cm$table["0", "0"]
  FP <- cm$table["1", "0"]
  FN <- cm$table["0", "1"]
  
  num <- (TP * TN) - (FP * FN)
  den <- sqrt(as.numeric(TP + FP) * as.numeric(TP + FN) * 
              as.numeric(TN + FP) * as.numeric(TN + FN))
  
  mcc_val <- ifelse(den == 0, 0, num / den)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model            = "Random Forest",
    Approach         = label,
    Threshold        = round(threshold, 4),
    Sensitivity      = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Specificity      = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 4),
    MCC              = round(mcc_val, 4),
    Overall_Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4),
    ROC_AUC          = round(pROC::auc(roc_rf), 4)
  )
}

rf_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  get_rf_metrics(test_rf_probs, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, 0.5000, "1. Baseline (p = 0.50)"),
  get_rf_metrics(test_rf_probs, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, opt_thresh_rf, "2. Youden J Threshold")
)

print(as.data.frame(rf_results))
```

#XGBoosting
```{r}
library(xgboost)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

#define complete feature matrix (6 transformed continuous + 4 binary predictors)
features <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
              "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium",
              "high_blood_pressure", "anaemia", "diabetes", "smoking")

X_train <- as.matrix(train_df[, features])
y_train <- train_df$DEATH_EVENT

X_test  <- as.matrix(test_df[, features])
y_test  <- test_df$DEATH_EVENT

#convert to dmatrix format
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
dtest  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test, label = y_test)

# 3. Calculate class imbalance weight ratio: (negative cases / positive cases)
scale_pos_weight_val <- sum(y_train == 0) / sum(y_train == 1)
cat("Class Imbalance Ratio (scale_pos_weight):", round(scale_pos_weight_val, 2), "\n")

set.seed(42)

#define hyperparameter grid
hyper_grid <- expand.grid(
  max_depth = c(2, 3, 4),
  eta = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1),
  subsample = c(0.7, 0.8, 1.0),
  colsample_bytree = c(0.7, 0.8, 1.0),
  best_nrounds = 0,
  test_auc = 0
)

#robust cross validation loop
for(i in 1:nrow(hyper_grid)) {
  params <- list(
    booster          = "gbtree",
    objective        = "binary:logistic",
    eval_metric      = "auc",
    max_depth        = hyper_grid$max_depth[i],
    eta              = hyper_grid$eta[i],
    subsample        = hyper_grid$subsample[i],
    colsample_bytree = hyper_grid$colsample_bytree[i],
    scale_pos_weight = scale_pos_weight_val
  )
  
  xgb_cv <- xgb.cv(
    params                = params,
    data                  = dtrain,
    nrounds               = 300,
    nfold                 = 5,
    early_stopping_rounds = 30,
    verbose               = FALSE,
    stratified            = TRUE
  )
  
  #safeguard against NULL best_iteration if early stopping isn't triggered
  best_iter <- ifelse(is.null(xgb_cv$best_iteration), 300, xgb_cv$best_iteration)
  
  hyper_grid$best_nrounds[i] <- best_iter
  hyper_grid$test_auc[i]     <- max(xgb_cv$evaluation_log$test_auc_mean)
}

#select best performing parameters
best_params <- hyper_grid[which.max(hyper_grid$test_auc), ]
cat("=== OPTIMAL XGBOOST HYPERPARAMETERS ===\n")
print(best_params)

#fit final model on full training set using optimal hyperparameters
final_params <- list(
  booster          = "gbtree",
  objective        = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric      = "auc",
  max_depth        = best_params$max_depth,
  eta              = best_params$eta,
  subsample        = best_params$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_params$colsample_bytree,
  scale_pos_weight = scale_pos_weight_val
)

xgb_fit <- xgb.train(
  params  = final_params,
  data    = dtrain,
  nrounds = best_params$best_nrounds
)

#predict probabilities on test set
test_xgb_probs <- predict(xgb_fit, dtest)

#roc and optimal threshold (youden's j)
roc_xgb <- pROC::roc(y_test, test_xgb_probs, quiet = TRUE)
opt_thresh_xgb <- pROC::coords(roc_xgb, "best", best.method = "youden")$threshold

#performance function (calculates MCC directly from the confusion matrix)
get_xgb_metrics <- function(probs, actual, threshold, label) {
  preds <- ifelse(probs >= threshold, 1, 0)
  cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(
    factor(preds, levels = c(0, 1)),
    factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1)),
    positive = "1"
  )
  
  #extract confusion matrix components for MCC
  TP <- cm$table["1", "1"]
  TN <- cm$table["0", "0"]
  FP <- cm$table["1", "0"]
  FN <- cm$table["0", "1"]
  
  num <- (TP * TN) - (FP * FN)
  den <- sqrt(as.numeric(TP + FP) * as.numeric(TP + FN) * 
              as.numeric(TN + FP) * as.numeric(TN + FN))
  
  mcc_val <- ifelse(den == 0, 0, num / den)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model            = "XGBoost",
    Approach         = label,
    Threshold        = round(threshold, 4),
    Sensitivity      = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Specificity      = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 4),
    MCC              = round(mcc_val, 4),
    Overall_Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4),
    ROC_AUC          = round(pROC::auc(roc_xgb), 4)
  )
}

xgb_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  get_xgb_metrics(test_xgb_probs, y_test, 0.5000, "1. Baseline (p = 0.50)"),
  get_xgb_metrics(test_xgb_probs, y_test, opt_thresh_xgb, "2. Youden J Threshold")
)

cat("=== XGBOOST TEST PERFORMANCE ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(xgb_results))
```

#Multivariate Outlier Analysis anad Model Sensitivy Check
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
library(xgboost)
library(tibble)

#continuous variables
cont_vars <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
               "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium")

X_cont <- train_df[, cont_vars]

#compute mean vector and covariance matrix
center_vec <- colMeans(X_cont)
cov_mat    <- cov(X_cont)

#calculate mahalanobis Distance for each observation
m_dist <- mahalanobis(X_cont, center = center_vec, cov = cov_mat)

#critical value threshold (chi-Square with df = 6, alpha = 0.01)
p_val <- 0.01
critical_val <- qchisq(1 - p_val, df = length(cont_vars))

#add results to dataframe
train_df_outliers <- train_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    mahal_dist = m_dist,
    is_outlier = m_dist > critical_val,
    p_value    = pchisq(m_dist, df = length(cont_vars), lower.tail = FALSE)
  )

num_outliers <- sum(train_df_outliers$is_outlier)
cat("=== MULTIVARIATE OUTLIER DETECTION (MAHALANOBIS DISTANCE) ===\n")
cat("Degrees of Freedom          :", length(cont_vars), "\n")
cat("Critical Threshold (p=0.01):", round(critical_val, 3), "\n")
cat("Multivariate Outliers      :", num_outliers, "(", round(num_outliers / nrow(train_df) * 100, 2), "% of training data)\n\n")

#display detected multivariate outliers
if(num_outliers > 0) {
  print(train_df_outliers %>% 
          dplyr::filter(is_outlier) %>% 
          dplyr::select(DEATH_EVENT, mahal_dist, p_value, inv_serum_creatinine, ejection_fraction, age))
}

#visualize outliers
ggplot(train_df_outliers, aes(x = seq_along(mahal_dist), y = mahal_dist, color = is_outlier)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = critical_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#2b5c8f", "TRUE" = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(
    title = "Multivariate Outlier Detection via Mahalanobis Distance",
    subtitle = paste0("Cutoff Threshold (df=6, alpha=0.01): ", round(critical_val, 2)),
    x = "Observation Index (Training Data)",
    y = "Mahalanobis Distance",
    color = "Outlier"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

#clean training set
train_df_clean <- train_df_outliers %>% dplyr::filter(!is_outlier)

#refit with outliers removed

#bic model clean
bic_clean_model <- glm(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ inv_serum_creatinine + age + ejection_fraction,
  data = train_df_clean,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

#aic model clean
aic_clean_model <- glm(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ inv_serum_creatinine + age + ejection_fraction + 
                high_blood_pressure + inv_serum_creatinine:ejection_fraction + 
                age:ejection_fraction,
  data = train_df_clean,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

#random forest clean
#prepare clean dataset for random forest (factor outcome required)
train_df_rf_clean <- train_df_clean
train_df_rf_clean$DEATH_EVENT <- factor(ifelse(train_df_clean$DEATH_EVENT == 1, "Died", "Survived"), 
                                       levels = c("Survived", "Died"))

set.seed(42)
rf_clean_fit <- randomForest(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ age + cpk_pow_neg02 + ejection_fraction + sqrt_platelets + 
                inv_serum_creatinine + serum_sodium + high_blood_pressure + 
                anaemia + diabetes + smoking,
  data = train_df_rf_clean,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

#xgboost clean
features <- c("age", "cpk_pow_neg02", "ejection_fraction", 
              "sqrt_platelets", "inv_serum_creatinine", "serum_sodium",
              "high_blood_pressure", "anaemia", "diabetes", "smoking")

X_train_clean <- as.matrix(train_df_clean[, features])
y_train_clean <- train_df_clean$DEATH_EVENT
dtrain_clean  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train_clean, label = y_train_clean)

scale_pos_weight_clean <- sum(y_train_clean == 0) / sum(y_train_clean == 1)

final_params_clean <- list(
  booster          = "gbtree",
  objective        = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric      = "auc",
  max_depth        = best_params$max_depth,
  eta              = best_params$eta,
  subsample        = best_params$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_params$colsample_bytree,
  scale_pos_weight = scale_pos_weight_clean
)

set.seed(42)
xgb_clean_fit <- xgb.train(
  params  = final_params_clean,
  data    = dtrain_clean,
  nrounds = best_params$best_nrounds
)

#coefficient comparisons post update
cat("\n=== CHAMPION BIC MODEL (FULL TRAINING DATA) ===\n")
print(summary(best_model_bic)$coefficients)

cat("\n=== CHAMPION BIC MODEL (REMOVED MULTIVARIATE OUTLIERS) ===\n")
print(summary(bic_clean_model)$coefficients)

cat("\n======================================================================\n")

cat("\n=== AIC MODEL (FULL TRAINING DATA) ===\n")
print(summary(best_model_aic)$coefficients)

cat("\n=== AIC MODEL (REMOVED MULTIVARIATE OUTLIERS) ===\n")
print(summary(aic_clean_model)$coefficients)

#youdens optimization
eval_sens_model <- function(probs, actual, label) {
  roc_obj    <- pROC::roc(actual, probs, quiet = TRUE)
  opt_thresh <- pROC::coords(roc_obj, "best", best.method = "youden")$threshold
  preds      <- ifelse(probs >= opt_thresh, 1, 0)
  
  cm <- caret::confusionMatrix(
    factor(preds, levels = c(0, 1)),
    factor(actual, levels = c(0, 1)),
    positive = "1"
  )
  
  # Calculate MCC directly from confusion matrix
  TP <- cm$table["1", "1"]
  TN <- cm$table["0", "0"]
  FP <- cm$table["1", "0"]
  FN <- cm$table["0", "1"]
  
  num <- (TP * TN) - (FP * FN)
  den <- sqrt(as.numeric(TP + FP) * as.numeric(TP + FN) * 
              as.numeric(TN + FP) * as.numeric(TN + FN))
  
  mcc_val <- ifelse(den == 0, 0, num / den)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    Model            = label,
    Threshold        = round(opt_thresh, 4),
    ROC_AUC          = round(pROC::auc(roc_obj), 4),
    Sensitivity      = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 4),
    Specificity      = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 4),
    MCC              = round(mcc_val, 4),
    Overall_Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4)
  )
}

#test set predictions for full/clean models
probs_bic_full  <- predict(best_model_bic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
probs_bic_clean <- predict(bic_clean_model, newdata = test_df, type = "response")

probs_aic_full  <- predict(best_model_aic, newdata = test_df, type = "response")
probs_aic_clean <- predict(aic_clean_model, newdata = test_df, type = "response")

probs_rf_full   <- predict(rf_fit, newdata = test_df_rf, type = "prob")[, "Died"]
probs_rf_clean  <- predict(rf_clean_fit, newdata = test_df_rf, type = "prob")[, "Died"]

X_test_mat      <- as.matrix(test_df[, features])
dtest_mat       <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test_mat)
probs_xgb_full  <- predict(xgb_fit, dtest_mat)
probs_xgb_clean <- predict(xgb_clean_fit, dtest_mat)

#sensitivity analysis
sens_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  eval_sens_model(probs_bic_full,  test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "1. BIC Model (Full Data)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_bic_clean, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "2. BIC Model (Cleaned)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_aic_full,  test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "3. AIC Model (Full Data)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_aic_clean, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "4. AIC Model (Cleaned)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_rf_full,   test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "5. Random Forest (Full Data)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_rf_clean,  test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "6. Random Forest (Cleaned)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_xgb_full,  test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "7. XGBoost Benchmark (Full Data)"),
  eval_sens_model(probs_xgb_clean, test_df$DEATH_EVENT, "8. XGBoost Benchmark (Cleaned)")
)

cat("\n=== SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS PERFORMANCE COMPARISON (TEST SET) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(sens_summary))
```
